units.Isaiah 1:1: The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
units.Isaiah 1:2: Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
units.Isaiah 1:3: An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
units.Isaiah 1:4: Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
units.Isaiah 1:5: Why should you be struck again as you add lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart in grief.
units.Isaiah 1:6: From feet to head: for neither a wound nor a bruise nor an inflamed blow is there a poultice to apply, nor oil nor bandages.
units.Isaiah 1:7: Your land is deserted, your cities burned by fire. Your country—foreigners consume it before you; it has been deserted, overturned by foreign peoples.
units.Isaiah 1:8: Daughter Zion will be left like a tent in a vineyard, like a fruit-watcher’s shelter in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
units.Isaiah 1:9: If the Lord Sabaoth had not left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.
units.Isaiah 1:10: Hear the Lord’s word, rulers of Sodom! Attend to God’s law, people of Gomorrah!
units.Isaiah 1:11: “What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
units.Isaiah 1:12: not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
units.Isaiah 1:13: you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
units.Isaiah 1:14: and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
units.Isaiah 1:15: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
units.Isaiah 1:16: Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
units.Isaiah 1:17: Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
units.Isaiah 1:18: Come, let us reason together, says the Lord. Though your sins are like purple-red, I will whiten them like snow; though they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.
units.Isaiah 1:19: If you are willing and listen to Me, you will eat the land’s good things.
units.Isaiah 1:20: But if you are unwilling and do not listen to Me, a sword will devour you, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.”
units.Isaiah 1:21: How the faithful city Zion has become a prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness lay at rest, but now murderers!
units.Isaiah 1:22: Your silver is unapproved; your retailers mix the wine with water.
units.Isaiah 1:23: Your rulers disobey, partners of thieves, loving gifts and pursuing repayment, not judging for orphans and not attending to widows’ judgment.
units.Isaiah 1:24: Therefore thus says the Master, the Lord Sabaoth: “Woe, mighty ones of Israel! For My anger will not cease among My opponents, and I will exact judgment from My enemies.
units.Isaiah 1:25: I will bring My hand against you and burn you to purity. I will destroy the disobedient, remove all lawless people from you and humble all the arrogant.
units.Isaiah 1:26: I will establish your judges as before and your counselors as at the beginning. After these things you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful Metropolis Zion.
units.Isaiah 1:27: For her captivity will be saved through judgment and through mercy.
units.Isaiah 1:28: The lawless and sinners will be shattered together, and those abandoning the Lord will be brought to an end.
units.Isaiah 1:29: For they will be ashamed of their idols, which they themselves wanted, and they were disgraced by their gardens, which they desired.
units.Isaiah 1:30: For they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, like a garden that has no water.
units.Isaiah 1:31: Their strength will become a stalk of tow and their works sparks of fire. The lawless and sinners will be burned together, with no one to quench.”
units.Isaiah 2:1: The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
units.Isaiah 2:2: In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,
units.Isaiah 2:3: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.
units.Isaiah 2:4: He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
units.Isaiah 2:5: And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!
units.Isaiah 2:6: For He abandoned His people, Israel’s house, because their country was filled, as from the beginning, with omens like the foreigners’ country, and many foreign children were born to them.
units.Isaiah 2:7: For their country was filled with silver and gold, and their treasures had no number; the land was filled with horses, and their chariots had no number.
units.Isaiah 2:8: The land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they bowed before what their fingers made.
units.Isaiah 2:9: A human being bowed down, and a man was humbled; I will certainly not let them go.
units.Isaiah 2:10: And now enter the rocks and hide in the earth from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.

units.Isaiah 2:14: against every mountain and every high hill,
units.Isaiah 2:15: against every high tower and every high wall,
units.Isaiah 2:16: against every ship of the sea and every beautiful display of ships.
units.Isaiah 2:17: Every human being will be humbled, humanity’s height will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
units.Isaiah 2:18: They will hide away all the handmade things,
units.Isaiah 2:19: carrying them into caves, into clefts in the rocks and into holes in the earth, from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
units.Isaiah 2:20: For on that day a person will cast out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to worship, to the worthless ones and the bats,
units.Isaiah 2:21: to enter holes in the solid rock and clefts in the rocks from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
